title: Inverclyde registered mortality: wider context for a Greenock-focused study

greenock.message: These are Inverclyde council outcomes; no Greenock-specific outcome is available

source.definition: Registered deaths meeting the NRS drug misuse definition: selected mental/behavioural drug-use ICD-10 causes, or specified poisoning causes with a controlled drug present; NRS exclusions apply. Not all drug poisonings or Police Scotland suspected deaths.
source.geographic_allocation: NRS-assigned council area in Table_C1; no locality allocation or GIS boundary crosswalk inferred
source.territorial_qualification: Workbook cover describes deaths occurring in Scotland, including persons usually resident outside Scotland; do not assert resident-only local incidence
source.rates: Table_C4, Notes note 1 and note 9: published five-year ASR, 2013 ESP, revised population vintages; annual council denominator absent
source.rate_vintage_note: Notes note 9 records rebased 2011–2022 populations and revised 2023 estimates; no attempt to recompute with a different population vintage
source.revisions: Frozen 2024 publication vintage; later NRS editions may revise counts/rates. Not the latest release; no later observations appended
cross_checks: 30 Persons counts checked against male+female cells where observed
22 five-year totals matched complete C1 windows

hierarchy.interpretation: Evidence scopes, not interchangeable GIS polygons or a population allocation crosswalk

levels.finding: No Greenock-specific mortality/toxicity outcome is inferred
Annual registered drug misuse deaths and published five-year ASRs
Legacy quarterly suspected deaths, separate indicator and boundary
Weekly ambulance naloxone and monthly treatment urine detections, not council outcomes
Same C1 registered definition and C4 published ASR; national total includes Inverclyde

rules: Never downscale wider-area counts or rates to Greenock
Never merge registered and suspected deaths or use a health-board population for a council
No implied substance-specific toxicity mechanism from all-drug registered counts

display_rules: Draw gaps for missing values; never zero-fill
Label trailing means by their ending year; NRS published five-year rates by full period
Do not label multi-year ASRs as annual crude rates
Show published confidence intervals and count/sampling/vintage caveats
Keep suspected-death/police and health-board contexts in separate indicator sections
No current threat colour, Greenock hotspot, clinical alert or significance inferred

local_anomaly_feasibility.reason: Sparse annual 10–33 counts with trend and one revised vintage. A ten-year reference leaves only five targets; no externally validated local event labels or chosen annual null model.
local_anomaly_feasibility.interpretation: Peaks, changes and published rate intervals are descriptive; none is a statistically detected anomaly or warning

limitations: Council outcomes cannot be assigned to Greenock
Counts are registrations, not exact event dates or all drug-attributable harm
NRS exclusions, classification and toxicology ascertainment can affect historical comparisons
No annual local crude rate or population-adjusted risk inferred from counts
Published five-year ASRs/intervals are imported, not independently recomputed; overlapping periods and nested geographies are dependent
Frozen 2024 vintage is not the latest NRS edition; no later counts appended
No model-generated local warning, causal substance inference or FOI-alert validation
